categories.name: Problem Framing
categories.description: How well the candidate defines and scopes the problem

levels.1: No clear problem definition; jumps straight to solutions
levels.2: Vague problem statement; misses key constraints or context
levels.3: Basic problem definition with some constraints identified
levels.4: Clear problem statement with constraints, users, and scope defined
levels.5: Exceptional framing with comprehensive problem analysis, stakeholder mapping, and success criteria

categories.name: Ideation Breadth
categories.description: Ability to generate multiple diverse solutions before converging

levels.1: Single solution proposed without exploring alternatives
levels.3: Three or more solutions with basic trade-off analysis
levels.4: Diverse solution space explored with clear selection criteria
levels.5: Creative ideation with unique approaches, systematic evaluation, and principled convergence

categories.name: Systems Thinking
categories.description: Understanding of user flows, edge cases, and error states

levels.1: Only considers happy path; no edge cases
levels.2: Acknowledges edge cases exist but doesn't address them
levels.3: Identifies some edge cases and basic error states
levels.4: Comprehensive flow mapping with error handling and recovery
levels.5: Deep systems analysis including state management, failure modes, and scalability

categories.name: Low-Fidelity Wireframing
categories.description: Quality and clarity of visual representations

levels.1: No visual artifacts or illegible sketches
levels.2: Basic shapes with no hierarchy or labels
levels.3: Recognizable UI elements with some labeling
levels.4: Clear wireframes with information hierarchy and component annotations
levels.5: Professional-quality wireframes with interaction annotations, responsive considerations, and clear flow

categories.name: UI/UX Pattern Knowledge
categories.description: Familiarity with standard design patterns and components

levels.2: Knows basic components (button, input) but limited vocabulary
levels.3: Uses proper component names (modal, dropdown, toast, accordion)
levels.4: References advanced patterns (lazy loading, infinite scroll, skeleton screens)
levels.5: Expert vocabulary including interaction patterns, accessibility considerations, and platform-specific conventions

levels.1: No prioritization; tries to solve everything
levels.2: Mentions priority but no clear framework
levels.3: Basic MVP definition with some rationale
levels.5: Strategic scoping with phased rollout plan and success metrics

categories.name: Metrics & Success Definition
categories.description: Ability to define and measure success

levels.1: No mention of metrics or success criteria
levels.2: Vague success statements like 'users will like it'
levels.5: Comprehensive metrics framework with leading/lagging indicators and experimentation plan

categories.name: Communication Clarity
categories.description: How clearly the candidate articulates their thinking

levels.1: Incoherent or jumbled thoughts; hard to follow
levels.5: Exceptional clarity with storytelling, analogies, and logical flow

feedback_instructions.strengths: Identify 2-3 specific moments where the candidate demonstrated strong skills
feedback_instructions.improvements: Identify 2-3 specific areas with actionable advice for improvement
feedback_instructions.drills: Suggest practice exercises tailored to the lowest-scoring categories
